subject: Phased handoff and ephemeral residency windows — SLA addendum Q&A
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@northbridgepharma.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@northbridgepharma.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Phased handoff windows — clarification for SLA addendum

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week. We are finalizing the security annex and need to lock the residency + deletion language for regulated PII in our pilot. Two quick clarifications so we can move to legal review:

1) Phased handoff: can Redwood commit to a staged return-of-data followed by secure wipe? Example request: 30d ephemeral residency for inference cache, then 7d post-handback retention for troubleshooting, then cryptographic wipe. Is that a supported pattern?

2) Time to verified deletion: how do you measure and certify that KV caches and ephemeral logs are irrecoverable? We will need an auditable statement for the order form.

We attached our template language. Can you confirm whether the proposed flow is feasible and what the SLA addendum would look like?

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Privacy & Vendor Risk
Northbridge Pharma

--- Attachment: NBP_SLA_Addendum_v1.0.pdf (PDF, 142 KB)

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@northbridgepharma.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Phased handoff windows — clarification for SLA addendum

Hi Priya — great questions. Short answers up front, then details below:

- Yes, we support a phased handback + secure wipe pattern (ephemeral cache -> short troubleshooting hold -> verified cryptographic wipe).
- Verified deletion is provided via a multi-step attest process (wipe job logs + SHA-256 snapshot of overwritten blocks) and can be included in the addendum.

Details / proposal:
• Proposed flow we can put in the order form:
  - Step A (Ephemeral residency): inference cache retained up to 30 days after ingestion.
  - Step B (Post-handback troubleshooting window): upon customer-triggered handback, Redwood will retain a restricted-access troubleshooting window of up to 7 days.
  - Step C (Final wipe + attestation): within 72 hours after the troubleshooting window ends, Redwood executes a cryptographic wipe of ephemeral KV caches and issues an attestation PDF with job IDs and checksums.

• Measurement and proof: we will supply job timestamps, wipe job IDs, and a signed attestation file that references the affected GPU host IDs and storage object IDs. For regulated customers we can include the attestation in the order form as a deliverable.

I attached a draft addendum and a short playbook that maps the flow to our operational runbook. Lauren — can you please review the 7-day troubleshooting hold language for our standard support escalation path?

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Director
Redwood Inference

--- Attachments: NBP_SLA_Addendum_v1.1.pdf (draft, 128 KB); phased-wipe-playbook.xlsx (spreadsheet, 54 KB)

Adding a couple of pragmatic notes from Support side:

- The 7-day troubleshooting hold is fine but we recommend a scoped access policy: only named CS/SEs with timebound sudo can access ephemeral snapshots. We'll enumerate roles in the addendum.
- If Northbridge needs a longer hold for regulatory review, we can support up to 14 days with an amended order form and pricing impact (extra retention = billable).
- We should clarify what "handback" trigger looks like (customer API call vs signed DocuSign), otherwise timeline disputes pop up.

Happy to align on exact wording — I flagged the relevant clause in the attached PDF.

-Lauren
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: priya.sharma@northbridgepharma.com <priya.sharma@northbridgepharma.com>

Subject: Re: Phased handoff windows — clarification for SLA addendum

Thanks — that aligns with our compliance expectations. A couple follow-ups:

1) Can Redwood commit to providing the attestation within 5 business days of the wipe job completion? We need a short SLA on attestation delivery.
2) Please add an explicit statement that backups/snapshots beyond ephemeral cache are not covered by this flow (we will manage backups separately).
3) For the "handback trigger" we prefer a signed DocuSign action from our Security Lead. Can you include DocuSign as an allowed trigger in the addendum?

If you can send the revised addendum with those three items we can loop in our legal for signature.

Best,
Priya

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Phased handoff windows — clarification for SLA addendum

Priya — thanks. Marcus reviewed and suggested final clause language, see below. I attached the redlined addendum (NBP_SLA_Addendum_v1.2.pdf) to this thread and included the DocuSign flow link.

Key additions in plain language we will include in v1.2:
• Attestation SLA: Redwood will deliver a signed attestation within 5 business days of successful wipe job completion. The attestation will include wipe job IDs, host IDs, and a signed SHA-256 summary.
• Backups exclusion: The addendum explicitly states that long-term backups and disaster-recovery snapshots are out-of-scope for this ephemeral wipe flow unless otherwise agreed in writing.
• Handback trigger: DocuSign-signed handback is an accepted trigger. The order form will enumerate API and DocuSign triggers and default to the most recent trigger event.

Next steps:
1) I will upload the redline to DocuSign and send to Priya's Legal & Security contacts as a pre-signed envelope for approval (link: https://docusign.com/NDx-7892).
2) If Northbridge requires the 14-day exception, we will add pricing and reissue.

If this looks good I'll mark the addendum ready for signature and route to finance.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Director
Redwood Inference
